main.title: Population – scenario
main.heading: Population — {name}
main.help.tip: Opens the help page of the tab shown.
main.open.tip.title: Open…
main.open.tip: Loads a scenario file (.json) saved earlier.
main.save.tip.title: Save…
main.save.tip: Saves every setting to a .json file, to run exactly the same calculation later.
scenario.name: Name
scenario.name.tip.title: Name
scenario.name.tip: Used in the report and in the name of the result layer group.
scenario.language.tip.title: Report language
scenario.language.tip: Language of the report and table headers. File names stay in English.
scenario.output.tip.title: Output folder
scenario.output.tip: Each run is written in a dated sub-folder (for example 2026-09-29_144805): no result is ever overwritten. Runs that are not kept can be deleted at the end of the session.
grid.cell_size.tip.title: Cell size
grid.cell_size.tip: 250 m by default. Larger for a quick first run over a large extent; rarely below 250 m (several buildings per cell).
grid.density_unit.tip.title: Density unit
grid.density_unit.tip: Unit of the densities entered and published. The calculation stays consistent whatever the unit.
grid.crs.tip.title: Calculation CRS
grid.crs.tip: Always projected, in metres: areas are computed in m². Layers may use any CRS, they are reprojected. A CRS in degrees is refused. Above 0.5 % of area distortion, an equal-area CRS is recommended.
crs.project_not_metric: The project CRS is not in metres: the tool will use the raster's if metric, otherwise the UTM zone of the study area.
data.study_area.tip.title: Study area
data.study_area.tip: Administrative boundaries of the area to simulate.
data.typology.tip.title: Typology and class field
data.typology.tip: Layer of zones (rural, urban, high-end…) and the field holding the class. Class names are free.
data.admin_units.tip.title: Administrative units
data.admin_units.tip: Optional. For balances by unit and recalibration on projections.
data.parameter_zones.tip.title: Parameter zones
data.parameter_zones.tip: Optional. When growth rates or maximum densities follow boundaries other than the typology.
data.raster.tip.title: Population raster
data.raster.tip: Raster at the base year, in any coordinate system (reprojected without losing inhabitants).
data.value_type.tip.title: Raster content
data.value_type.tip: Density (like the BUR71 raster) or inhabitants per pixel (like WorldPop). A mix-up would bias everything by the pixel area.
data.boundary.tip.title: Boundary pixels
data.boundary.tip: A pixel across the study-area boundary is cut: only the area inside is counted.
data.roofs.tip.title: Roofs (buildings)
data.roofs.tip: Google Open Buildings, PostGIS, GeoPackage… Used by the calibration (phase 6).
data.exclusions.tip.title: Exclusion zones
data.exclusions.tip: Forests, lakes, military areas, dams… as many layers as needed.
data.exclusions.name: Name
data.exclusions.behaviour.tip.title: Behaviour
data.exclusions.behaviour.tip: No inflow: its inhabitants stay, its growth moves elsewhere. Relocate: all its inhabitants move (dam). Outside: removed (other country, lake).
data.projections.file.tip.title: CSV file
data.projections.file.tip: Columns admin, year, population: totals by administrative unit and year.
data.projections.use.tip.title: Use
data.projections.use.tip: Comparison only, yearly recalibration, or start on a projection year.
data.projections.start_year.tip.title: Start year
data.projections.start_year.tip: Only used when starting on a projection year.
time.base_year.tip.title: Base year
time.base_year.tip: Year of the base population (census year).
time.end_year.tip.title: Final horizon
time.time_step.tip.title: Time step
time.time_step.tip: 10, 5, 1 year or less. Output years are always reached exactly.
time.output_years.tip.title: Output years
time.output_years.tip: Years for which maps are written. Empty: at the end of every step.
time.frequency.tip.title: Migration
time.frequency.tip: Every year: better distribution. Once per step: faster, for a first try; reported.
time.first_migration_year.tip.title: First migration
time.first_migration_year.tip: Before this year, only growth applies.
parameters.box.tip.title: Growth rates and maximum densities
parameters.box.tip: One row per class or zone ("*": default). A constant value, or values at pivot years, interpolated linearly.
parameters.key.tip.title: Class / zone
parameters.key.tip: Typology class name, parameter-zone identifier, or "*" for the default value.
parameters.extrapolation.tip.title: Beyond the years
parameters.extrapolation.tip: Before the first and after the last pivot year: constant value, or linear extension.
parameters.note: Growth rate in % per year; maximum densities in the chosen unit (Scenario tab).
migration.k.tip.title: Neighbours
migration.k.tip: The excess of a cell goes in equal shares to the N nearest cells with free room.
migration.tolerance.tip.title: Tolerance (inhabitants)
migration.tolerance.tip: Minimal excess, in whole inhabitants, that triggers a move. No-inflow zones export all their excess.
migration.policy.tip.title: When room runs out
migration.policy.tip: What to do when the population no longer fits. See the help page on non-convergence.
migration.max_auto_increase.tip.title: Max automatic increase
migration.max_auto_increase.tip: Increase of maximum densities accepted without asking (0 %: always ask).
migration.sink_width_cells.tip.title: Ring width (cells)
migration.sink_width_cells.tip: Width of the ring of sink cells around the study area.
water.enabled.tip.title: Compute drinking-water demand
water.enabled.tip: Adds maps and totals of consumption, mean production, peak day and peak hour.
water.water_per_capita.tip.title: Allowance (l/cap/d)
water.water_per_capita.tip: Domestic consumption per inhabitant and per day.
water.non_domestic_share.tip.title: Non-domestic (%)
water.non_domestic_share.tip: Schools, health, shops… as % of domestic consumption.
water.non_domestic_volume.tip.title: Fixed volume (m³/d)
water.non_domestic_volume.tip: Fixed non-domestic needs of the zone, shared pro rata population.
water.network_efficiency.tip.title: Efficiency (%)
water.network_efficiency.tip: Network efficiency: applies to daily demand, not to the peak hour.
water.peak_day_factor.tip.title: Peak day
water.peak_hour_factor.tip.title: Peak hour
water.note: A value, or values by year: "2026: 20; 2040: 30".
indicators.other: Other uses (waste, energy, school places…) can be added here the same way.
calibration.phase6: The roof area → population calibration (regressions by stratum, manual adjustment, diagnostics) comes in phase 6. Meanwhile, the base population comes from a raster (Data tab).
run.run.tip.title: Run
run.run.tip: Checks the scenario and runs it in the background.
run.error: The run could not start: see the log.
run.status.success_with_adjustments: Run successful with adjustments (see the report).
run.status.partial: Partial run: part of the population could not be placed.
results.load.tip.title: Load layers
results.load.tip: Adds the checked maps to the project, in one group per scenario, with ready-made styles.
report.none: No report yet: run a scenario first.
nc.title: Not enough room in {year}
nc.raise: Raise maximum densities by {increase} % (minimum: {minimal} %), also for the following years
nc.sink: Place the excess in a ring of sink cells around the study area
nc.unallocated: Record the excess as unallocated population and go on
nc.note: The run restarts from the beginning with the chosen solution, which is recorded in the scenario and the report.
help.title: Help — Population
about.title: About Poplar
about.text:
Poplar — population growth and migration

Projects the spatial distribution of population year after year, by growth and migration under density constraints, and translates it into needs (drinking water…).

Version {version}
Origin: SHER tool (QGIS model and PyQGIS script), rebuilt in 2026 for project BUR71.
Authors: original tool, Keyvan; rebuild, Michel, with AI-assisted development (to be confirmed).
Method: code validated by automated tests and by comparison with the original tool.
Organisation, licence, contact: to be confirmed.
Dependencies: none beyond QGIS.

Project repository
processing.run.name: Run a scenario
processing.run.help: Runs a Poplar scenario file (.json): growth, migration and indicators from the base year to the final horizon. Results (rasters, summary.csv table, report) are written to the scenario's output folder or to the folder given.
processing.run.load: Load the final population and density
results.run.tip.title: Run shown
results.run.tip: Each run has its own folder. Choose the one whose maps, table and report you want to see.
results.kept.tip.title: Keep
results.kept.tip: A kept run is never proposed for deletion.
results.label.tip.title: Run name
results.label.tip: A short name to find it again, for example “reference” or “dmax + 20 %”.
results.clean.tip.title: Clean up
results.clean.tip: Deletes in one go the runs that are not kept.
cleanup.title: Clean-up of the results
cleanup.intro: Runs saved in {folder}. The runs checked in “Delete” are erased with their files; their layers are first removed from the project.
cleanup.intro_end: End of session: these runs take up space in {folder}. Check “Keep” to keep a run; the other checked runs will be deleted.
cleanup.all.tip.title: Check all
cleanup.all.tip: If no run is kept, the latest successful run stays unchecked.
cleanup.delete.tip.title: Delete selection
cleanup.delete.tip: Permanently erases the checked folders. Input data are never touched.
cleanup.failed:
Some files could not be deleted (open in another program?):
{files}
check.buffer_missing: Exclusion zone “{name}”: a layer of lines or points needs a buffer in metres (Data tab).
data.exclusions.buffer.tip.title: Buffer (m)
data.exclusions.buffer.tip: Width added around each feature, in metres. Required for a layer of lines (road, river) or points (borehole); optional for polygons, which it widens.
